skill.name: global-conventions
skill.description: Follow consistent project structure, version control practices, environment configuration, code review processes, and development conventions across the entire application. Use this skill when organizing project files and directories, when writing commit messages or creating pull requests, when managing environment variables and configuration, when participating in code reviews, when defining testing requirements, when using feature flags, when maintaining changelogs, when documenting setup instructions, or when establishing consistent development practices across the team.
skill.summary: Applies shared development conventions for structure, version control, configuration, reviews, testing, and releases.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is confirmed because SKILL.md directs the agent to follow a ../../../ path outside the skill directory. No prompt injection or malicious social engineering was found in the audited file, but the external relative reference creates a filesystem boundary and portability risk.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md references ../../../agent-os/standards/global/conventions.md outside the packaged skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Move the required conventions into the skill package or link to a package-local file without path traversal.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 28 instructs the agent to follow a ../../../ relative path that escapes the skill directory. This can load unbundled repository content and violates expected skill package boundaries.

high_findings.title: Path traversal sequence
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 28 instructs the agent to follow a ../../../ relative path that escapes the skill directory. This can load unbundled repository content and violates expected skill package boundaries.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when project structure, reviews, releases, and configuration rules are inconsistent. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a shared checklist for applying development conventions.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when project structure guidance should be applied.
Covers branch, commit, pull request, and changelog practices.
Includes environment configuration and dependency documentation topics.
Supports testing requirement and feature flag decisions.
Directs the assistant toward shared global convention guidance.
limitations: The detailed convention text is referenced outside the skill package.
It does not execute tests or validate repository policy automatically.
It does not include templates for every team workflow.
It depends on the host project having compatible standards.

use_cases.title: Normalize Repository Structure
use_cases.description: Apply consistent file and directory conventions before adding new modules or moving existing code.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reviewable Changes
use_cases.description: Check branches, commits, pull requests, tests, and changelog notes against shared team expectations.

use_cases.title: Document Team Practices
use_cases.description: Create setup, dependency, and contribution notes that match established development conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Conventions
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review before a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned change for project structure, commit message, test, and documentation conventions. List only issues I should fix first.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare this feature branch for review. Check branch naming, commits, tests, feature flags, changelog notes, and pull request content.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Configuration Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this configuration change for environment variable naming, documentation, dependency rationale, setup instructions, and safe rollout practices.

prompt_templates.title: Design Team Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare our proposed development workflow with the global conventions. Identify gaps in structure, reviews, testing, release notes, and contribution guidance.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether a new feature needs a flag, tests, and changelog entry.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a feature flag for incomplete behavior, targeted tests before merge, and a changelog note for user-visible changes.

output_examples.input: A team lead asks for review guidance before restructuring folders.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks naming consistency, ownership boundaries, documentation updates, and whether the pull request explains the migration.

output_examples.input: A contributor asks how to document a new dependency.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the dependency purpose, setup impact, alternatives considered, and any configuration needed by future maintainers.

best_practices: Use this skill before opening pull requests that change structure, setup, or release behavior.
Pair convention checks with actual repository tests and linters.
Keep team standards in the same package or repository path used by the skill.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the skill as a replacement for automated tests or policy checks.
Do not reference standards that are outside the installed skill package.
Do not apply conventions without checking the current repository context.

faq.question: What does this skill help standardize?
faq.answer: It guides project structure, version control, configuration, reviews, tests, feature flags, changelogs, and documentation practices.

faq.question: Does it make code changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that an assistant can apply while planning, reviewing, or editing repository work.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is the detailed standards document included?
faq.answer: No. The skill currently references a standards file outside the package, which should be bundled before publication.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Software engineers, feature developers, reviewers, and technical leads can use it to align development workflow decisions.

faq.question: Does it validate compliance?
faq.answer: No. It does not run tests, inspect policies automatically, or enforce repository rules by itself.
